cards.title: Rule 10 (skip-empty-bindings) lifted into universal grammar
cards.description: New Rule 10 in menu-input-interaction-grammar.md: focusable elements with no defined directional binding for an axis are SKIPPED during focus traversal in that axis -- focus does not stop on dead nodes. cards.title: Engine Phase 2: thread pool + progress channel + boot overlay (verify still serial)
cards.description: SHIPPED 2026-05-03. New files: port/src/boot_pool.{h,c} (SDL_CreateThread-based pool, N=physical_cores-2 workers, floor 1, cap 16, pd.ini Boot.WorkerThreads override, GetLogicalProcessorInformation on Windows for accurate physical-core count); port/src/boot_progress.{h,c} (22-phase enum, thread-safe channel with internal SDL mutex, weight-based 0..1 overall progress); port/fast3d/pdgui_bootoverlay.cpp (plain bottom progress bar + phase label + status label, PD-themed via pdguiGetActivePaletteRaw, ImGui DrawList only no textures, eased fill so 2011-file verify renders smooth, dedicated-server no-op). Render plumbing: gfx_run_boot_overlay_frame helper added to port/fast3d/gfx_pc.cpp + gfx_api.h. Boot reorder: catalog work block (romdataInit through modmgrCatalogChanged) carved out of main() into bootRunCatalogWork on the pool worker; main thread drives pdguiBootOverlayPump at 60Hz until bootProgressIsComplete, then bootPoolWaitIdle + Shutdown trio + atexit + mempHeap as before. Per-file progress hooks added to romextract.c verify + extract loops (every 32 files for files, every segment for segs). sysLogPrintf wrapped in lazy SDL mutex so worker + main thread can log concurrently without corrupting s_LogRing. Verify pass STILL SERIAL (intentional per Phase 2 design); Phase 3 c109 will fan out per-file. Audit: context/audits/engine-phase2-thread-pool-overlay-2026-05-03.md.
cards.notes: Worktree silly-dijkstra-05e238. SHA pending. Spec at context/designs/engine/startup-acceleration.md Phase 2. Approved 2026-05-03 (Q1-Q6).

cards.title: Engine Phase 3: parallel verify pass
cards.description: SHIPPED 2026-05-03 at dev SHA 8554b4ea (worktree exciting-wozniak-fe0cac, two merges: e42ad24c implementation + 8554b4ea fixup). port/src/romextract.c now fans out romExtractVerifyAll across the boot pool's 14 workers (Mike's 16-core machine): shared next_file_num cursor with mutex pulled one file at a time, per-thread verify_thread_state_t accumulators, single mutex op per worker to merge counters + event list into shared verify_batch_t. Per-file SHA-256 + I/O is independent; failure events deferred to thread-local lists and replayed serially after the join so s_PerFileToastsEmitted cap stays correct (per-file LOUDFAIL log lines still fire from workers since sysLogPrintf is mutex-protected). Manager runs s_verifyWorkerFn inline (cannot bootPoolWaitIdle -- would deadlock on its own in_flight slot); per-batch latch (workers_remaining + cv_done) instead. Smoke verify on Mike's install: 0.23s -> 0.08s warm-cache (~3x); cold-cache projection per design doc 8s -> ~1s. test_romextract_passd.cpp toast assertion re-pinned for Phase 3 wiring. Audit: context/audits/engine-phase3-parallel-verify-2026-05-03.md.
cards.notes: SHIPPED 2026-05-03 at dev SHA 8554b4ea (worktree exciting-wozniak-fe0cac). Build verify clean four-target (client 55.5MB / server 22.4MB / updater 12.3MB / tests 24.6MB). Spec at context/designs/engine/startup-acceleration.md Phase 3.

cards.title: Engine Phase 4: walker + emitter structural concurrency
cards.description: SHIPPED 2026-05-03 (hardcore-leavitt-20fefd). Generic bootPoolForRangeBlocking helper in port/src/boot_pool.c: shared mutex-cursor + manager-runs-inline pattern from Phase 3 verify, exposed as a per-index fan-out API. Catalog mutex (single SDL_mutex in port/src/assetcatalog.c) wraps every public hot path that touches s_HashTable / s_EntryPool: register*, resolve, getMutable, hasEntry, isEnabled, set*, iterate*, getCount*, getByIndex, clear*, refresh. Typed register wrappers refactored to call new s_registerLocked under one critical section so the entry pointer + type-specific field fill stay valid across concurrent realloc. New helper assetCatalogSetCategoryById() for walker callbacks that fill e->category after register. loader_pool gets a single SDL_mutex around all parse* helpers + reset/finalize so concurrent walker callbacks serialize correctly into the shared arenas (s_GuncmdsUsed, s_AmmosUsed, etc.). loaderWalkerScanKind: collect-then-fan-out -- Phase 1 readdir + collect filenames into a heap array; Phase 2 fans per-file work across the boot pool, counters merge under a batch mutex. 12 emitters parallelized via bootPoolForRangeBlocking on their inner per-asset loops: pdwpn (86), pdmesh (two-phase upstream dedup, ~512 unique), pdanim (110), pdanim_chr (1208), pdhead (84), pdbody (68), pdarena (47, dual emit -> .pdarena + .pdscenario), pdsfx (1545), pdvoice (1545 filtered), pdsong (~119), pdfont (10), pdlang (68). The pdui emitter stays serial (GL render-loop trigger, not on the catalog work thread). Build verify clean four-target via build-session.ps1 -Session phase4: client 55.5 MB / updater 12.3 MB / server 22.4 MB / tests 24.6 MB.

cards.title: Engine Phase 5: polish + measurements
cards.description: SHIPPED 2026-05-03 (hardcore-leavitt-20fefd). Per-launch weight caching: const k_PhaseWeight[] becomes mutable s_PhaseWeights[] backed by 22 Boot.Weight.<phase> pd.ini keys; bootProgressMarkComplete recomputes per-phase fractions from SDL_GetTicks measurements captured between BeginPhase / EndPhase, configSave at shutdown writes them so the next boot's bar paces from real timings instead of hand-calibrated defaults. First-launch unchanged (pd.ini empty -> defaults stay). New Boot.Telemetry pd.ini int flag (default 0) emits a per-phase elapsed-ms log dump at end of boot when set; format: 'BOOT_TELEMETRY: total=<ms> workers=<N> phases:' followed by one line per non-skipped phase. Pool tuning: existing (cores - 2) formula verified (Mike's 16-core box -> 14 workers, floor 1 on minimal hardware). Overlay polish: no change -- Phase 2 overlay already eased + theme-driven + percentage-bearing per Mike's Q2. Build verify clean four-target via build-session.ps1 -Session phase5: client 55.5 MB / updater 12.3 MB / server 22.4 MB / tests 24.6 MB.

cards.title: B-323 post-boot AV in challengesInit (Pass C side-effect, N64-vs-PC stride)
cards.description: SHIPPED 2026-05-03 (competent-saha-a202bb). Mike's playtest of dev 1363ee75 AVs at boot inside challengesInit() -- bcopy/memcpy+146 from a dmaExecWithAutoAlign over-read in src/game/challenge.c::challengeLoadConfig. Root cause: PC sizeof(struct mpconfig) = 4596 and sizeof(struct mpstrings) = 680 used as both stride and read length, but on-disk segment is laid out with N64 sizes (mpstrings 320 bytes/entry); MAX_BOTS grew 8 -> 32. Pre-Pass-C the over-read landed in adjacent ROM bytes inside the contiguous 32 MB g_RomFile -- harmless. Post-Pass-C (S607, dev b15cc701) each segment is its own heap allocation; over-read AVs. g_MpChallenges[0].confignum=14 makes the very first call attempt a 4596-byte read at offset 14*4596=64344, ~60 KB past the 4576-byte segment. Fix: (1) Remove mpconfigs dmaExec entirely (data was always overwritten by mpconfig->config = g_MpConfigs[confignum] -- dead code). (2) Replace mpstrings dmaExec with bcopy of N64_MPSTRINGS_SIZE=320 bytes from confignum*320, into the head of the PC mpstrings struct (description[200] + aibotnames[0..7] = 320 bytes matches N64 layout exactly), with bzero of the whole PC struct first to leave aibotnames[8..31] zeroed. Bots 9..32 fall back to legacy g_BotConfigsArray naming. Build verify clean four-target via build-session.ps1 -Session b323: client 55.5 MB, updater 12.3 MB, server 22.4 MB, tests 24.6 MB. Audit append in context/audits/catalog-universality-pivot-plan-2026-05-02.md 'BYOR post-boot AV triaged' section. Bug ledger entry at B-323. Note: NOT a BYOR-completion issue -- this AV exists in BOTH pre-BYOR and post-BYOR builds; the user's prompt framing was inaccurate.
